prompt: Mostly realistic, like a period film still, but made with aerosol spray paint: every light has a soft overspray halo, the edges of the frame fade into fine spray mist and speckle, and thin drips run down from the brightest colours. Faces stay realistic and detailed. Camera low at the height of the firebox, fresh banknotes scattered on the stone floor in the foreground. In a hidden 1920s basement print room, a huge cast-iron printing press throws sheets of banknotes into the air. Beside it a tall skinny man in a bowler hat with a heavy gold mayoral chain round his neck, a long narrow face, hollow cheeks and a pencil-thin grey moustache, shovels coal into the press's red-hot firebox, grinning. Behind him an exhausted stoker in a soot-black vest sits slumped against the brick wall. Riveted pipes, brass gauges, steam. Key: one sodium-orange lamp overhead. The shadows are filled with electric violet spray mist. Most of the frame is dark; the brightest values are the lamp and the faces it catches. Plain margins with no writing. Thanks.
